fields.System.Title: RET-1 — Return authorisation
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Give a customer permission to send something back, with a reference the warehouse can match the
arriving parcel against.

Scope

In. RMA creation, quantity validation against what shipped, RMA queries, expiry.

Out. Refund calculation. Customer communication. Return shipping labels.

Design notes

An RMA is an expectation, exactly like an ASN. It never creates stock. Only a received and
inspected return does that.

Validate against what shipped, not what was ordered. An order for 10 that shipped 8 can
have at most 8 returned. This requires a cross-module call into outbound.

Orders shipped before go-live will not be found. That is not a bug to fix but a case to
handle — allow a blind return path with approval, and record an exception. See
[RET-202](../../stories/RET/RET-202-blind-return.md).

Expire unused RMAs. Otherwise the open list grows forever and stops being a useful view of
what is genuinely expected back.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Original order not found | [doc 05 WF 9](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
| Return quantity exceeding what shipped | [doc 05 WF 9](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
| RMA used twice | [doc 09 §8.4](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
